src/lib/rcap/documents/packet-route-reso: Import block: added factoryV2RouteMigrationFor and factoryV2RouteProductizationFor alongside the existing factoryV2RouteFor import.

Retired-jurisdiction fence: replaced the hoisted lookup `const exactFactoryRoute = factoryV2RouteFor(jurisdiction, pathwayId, input.trackId)` plus its two `exactFactoryRoute?.…` reads with the two exact accessors `factoryV2RouteMigrationFor(jurisdiction, pathwayId, input.trackId)` and `factoryV2RouteProductizationFor(jurisdiction, pathwayId, input.trackId)`, so the fence keeps its exact-migration and exact-productization escape hatches without the factory_v2 lookup running ahead of it. Comment added explaining why.

factory_v2 branch: `const factoryRoute = exactFactoryRoute` became `const factoryRoute = factoryV2RouteFor(jurisdiction, pathwayId, input.trackId)`, which is now the resolver's only factoryV2RouteFor call and sits after the component-deferral, exact-deferral, terminal-treatment, complete-guidance and LEGACY_VERIFIED checks. The branch body is untouched: it already set routeKind "factory_v2", sellable false, creditConsumable false and rendererKind packet_document_v1.
src/lib/rcap/documents/factory-v2-regist: Added factoryV2RouteProductizationFor(jurisdiction, pathwayId, trackId?), a three-line sibling of the existing factoryV2RouteMigrationFor that returns factoryV2RouteFor(...)?.exactRouteProductization ?? null. It exists because the fence needs the exact productization (DC misattributed arrest is a LEGACY_VERIFIED jurisdiction that passes the fence on a productization, not a migration) and the migration accessor alone could not supply it. No admission logic was changed; both accessors resolve the same admissible row.
scripts/verify-rcap-factory-v2-route.mjs: Fixed one demonstrably wrong expectation, with evidence. The B-block located the branch with resolver.indexOf("factoryV2RouteFor(jurisdiction, pathwayId)") — an exact two-argument call. Commit 07804aa68 (2026-09-04, 'Productize Illinois felony prostitution packet route') added the third argument the exact-track-selection contract requires, input.trackId, so from that commit the anchor never matched, indexOf returned -1 and slice(-1) made "the branch" the last character of the file. B-kind, B-sellable and B-credit were therefore reported against one character rather than against the branch, which sets all three. The argument is load-bearing: dropping it would both admit a route whose caller supplied a mismatched trackId and refuse a route whose registry row sets exactTrackSelectionRequired, i.e. it would change resolution outcomes, so the anchor cannot be satisfied as written. Re-anchored on "factoryV2RouteFor(" — the same prefix B-single and B-order already use — and made a missing call an empty branch rather than a one-character one, so B-branch can fire. No expectation was removed or loosened.
